To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
negativity and emotion are the most common dimensions in electoral campaigns, and they are also the dimensions that have the greatest effects on media attention.

negativity, emotionality and populism are all important dimensions of election campaigns; negativity and populism are more important than emotionality in presidential elections; negativity backlashes overall but personal attacks can be successful; appeals to enthusiasm (and not fear) can be used successfully in elections with many candidates; fear appeals are more likely to be effective in presidential elections.
negative, emotional and populist campaigning are more likely than positive campaigning to attract media attention and to increase the chances for an electoral victory.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of negativity in electoral campaigns has a backlash effect, and that the use of emotionality, in the form of both enthusiasm and fear appeals, is more likely to be effective, but only when the number of candidates is low and when the election is presidential, respectively.

the use of negativity and emotionality in electoral campaigns is widespread, and that it has a substantial impact on media attention and on electoral results, with some caveats.
negativity, emotionality and populism can all be used effectively by politicians to capture the attention and votes of the electorate.
